```{r setup, include = FALSE, purl = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>"
)
# the code of the benchmark is in scripts in the directory code (one to
# prepare the data, one to run the programs from the command line, with the
# scripts it runs for gt_radmix() and OpenADMIXTURE.jl, and one to run
# gt_radmix() in an R session), from which the chunks below are read
# (purl = FALSE because pkgdown purls this file from the package root when
# looking for images, where these relative paths do not exist)
knitr::read_chunk("code/admixture_benchmark_data.R")
knitr::read_chunk("code/admixture_benchmark_cli.sh")
knitr::read_chunk("code/admixture_benchmark_radmix_cli.R")
knitr::read_chunk("code/admixture_benchmark_openadmixture.jl")
knitr::read_chunk("code/admixture_benchmark_radmix.R")
knitr::read_chunk("code/admixture_benchmark_large_data.R")
knitr::read_chunk("code/admixture_benchmark_large_fit.R")
knitr::read_chunk("code/admixture_benchmark_large.sh")
# the directory with the results of the benchmark (data/admixture_benchmark,
# or data/admixture_benchmark_quick for the results of a quick run)
results_dir <- params$results_dir
```

`gt_radmix()` estimates ancestry proportions with the method of ADMIXTURE
(Alexander et al. 2009), directly from the backing file of a `gen_tibble`.
It uses the algorithm of ADMIXTURE (block-wise Newton updates with
quasi-Newton acceleration), in multithreaded C++, and the cross-validation
of ADMIXTURE (Alexander and Lange 2011). This article compares `gt_radmix()`
with four programs that fit the same model: ADMIXTURE itself, fastmixture
(Santander et al. 2024), ADAMIXTURE (Saurina-i-Ricos et al. 2026), and
OpenADMIXTURE.jl (Ko et al. 2023), a Julia implementation of the algorithm
of ADMIXTURE (run without its selection of ancestry informative markers).
OpenADMIXTURE.jl and ADAMIXTURE can also run on GPUs, which lets them scale
to biobank datasets; this comparison is limited to the CPU implementations
of the programs, which are all multithreaded. ADAMIXTURE also stores the
genotypes in a 2-bit packed encoding, which keeps its memory use low. For
very large datasets, some of the programs can therefore perform better than
this benchmark suggests.

The comparison uses the Human Genome Diversity Project (HGDP), and has two
parts:

- [Random starts](#random-starts): all the programs start from random
  values (ADMIXTURE and OpenADMIXTURE.jl have no other start, and
  fastmixture and ADAMIXTURE are run with their option to do so). It checks
  that the programs find the same ancestry proportions, and measures how
  long each takes on different numbers of cores, with and without
  cross-validation (which OpenADMIXTURE.jl does not have).
- [SVD and random starts](#svd-and-random-starts): `gt_radmix()`,
  fastmixture and ADAMIXTURE can also start from a truncated singular value
  decomposition (SVD) of the genotypes, which fastmixture and ADAMIXTURE do
  by default (`gt_radmix()` does so with `init = "svd"`). Each of them is run
  from both starts, with several seeds, to compare their times and the
  log-likelihoods they reach.

A last part, [Data larger than the memory](#data-larger-than-the-memory),
runs `gt_radmix()` alone on simulated data, with its memory capped below
their size, to show what working out of memory costs.

All the programs are timed from the command line, each run being a new
process that starts the program, reads the data and saves the results.
`gt_radmix()` is also timed in an R session, and OpenADMIXTURE.jl in a
Julia session, in which the package is already loaded (see
[How long do they take?](#how-long-do-they-take)).

The [results](#results) come first. The second part,
[How the benchmark was run](#how-the-benchmark-was-run), describes the data
and the runs, with their code, and how to run the benchmark again.

```{r read_results, include = FALSE}
  openadmixture = "OpenADMIXTURE.jl (Julia session)"
)
# the program of each of them
tool_program <- c(
  radmix_cli = "radmix", radmix = "radmix", admixture = "admixture",
  fastmixture = "fastmixture", adamixture = "adamixture",
  openadmixture_cli = "openadmixture", openadmixture = "openadmixture"
)
program_labels <- c(
  radmix = "gt_radmix()",
  admixture = "ADMIXTURE",

)
# one colour per program, in all the plots
program_colours <- c(

# one row per run, with its time, log-likelihood, cross-validation error
```

```{r align_q, include = FALSE}
# the Q matrix of a run, with 6 decimals (as written by ADMIXTURE and most
# of the other programs; ADAMIXTURE writes 18 significant digits)
read_q <- function(run) {
  round(
    as.matrix(read.table(file.path(results_dir, "Q", paste0(run, ".Q")))),
    6
  )
}
# all the permutations of 1:n, one per row
permutations <- function(n) {
  if (n == 1) {
    return(matrix(1L))
  }
  smaller <- permutations(n - 1)
  do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(n), function(first) {
    others <- setdiff(seq_len(n), first)
    cbind(first, matrix(others[smaller], ncol = n - 1))
  }))
}
# the clusters of different runs are numbered arbitrarily, so the columns of
# a Q matrix are reordered to best match those of a reference (with the
# smallest sum of squared differences, trying all the permutations)
align_q <- function(q, reference) {
  perms <- permutations(ncol(q))
  ssd <- apply(perms, 1, function(perm) sum((q[, perm] - reference)^2))
  unname(q[, perms[which.min(ssd), ]])
}
```

```{r agreement, include = FALSE}
# the reference: ADMIXTURE on the fewest cores, without cross-validation
min_cores <- min(timings$n_cores)
max_cores <- max(timings$n_cores)
reference_run <- paste0("admixture_t", min_cores, "_nocv")
q_ref <- read_q(reference_run)
k <- ncol(q_ref)
# the Q matrix of each run, with its clusters in the order of the reference
q_aligned <- lapply(
  setNames(timings$run, timings$run),
  function(run) align_q(read_q(run), q_ref)
)
max_diff <- function(a, b) max(abs(a - b))
rmse <- function(a, b) sqrt(mean((a - b)^2))
# for each run, the difference in log-likelihood from the reference, the
# largest difference in the ancestry proportions from the run of the same
# program on the fewest cores without cross-validation, and the RMSE and
# largest difference from the reference
agreement <- timings %>%
  mutate(
    own_run = paste0(tool, "_t", min_cores, "_nocv"),
    loglik_diff = loglik - loglik[run == reference_run],
    diff_own = mapply(
      function(run, own_run) max_diff(q_aligned[[run]], q_aligned[[own_run]]),
      run, own_run
    ),
    rmse_ref = vapply(run, function(r) rmse(q_aligned[[r]], q_ref), 0),
    diff_ref = vapply(run, function(r) max_diff(q_aligned[[r]], q_ref), 0)
  )
```

```{r numbers, include = FALSE}
# numbers for the text: the time of a run, the agreement of a program with
# ADMIXTURE (on the fewest cores, without cross-validation), and the largest
# difference between the runs of a program
time_of <- function(tool, n_cores = min_cores, crossval = FALSE) {
  timings$seconds[
    timings$tool == tool & timings$n_cores == n_cores &
      timings$crossval == crossval
  ]
}
# the cross-validation error of a program, on the fewest cores
cv_of <- function(tool) {
  formatC(
    timings$cv_error[
      timings$tool == tool & timings$n_cores == min_cores & timings$crossval
    ],
    format = "f", digits = 5
  )
}
format_seconds <- function(x) {
  trimws(formatC(signif(x, 3), format = "fg", digits = 3, big.mark = ","))
}
format_diff <- function(x) {
  ifelse(x == 0, "0", formatC(signif(x, 2), format = "fg", digits = 2))
}
# the range of several times (or amounts of memory, in MB, rounded to tens),
# e.g. "6.5-7.1", for programs whose runs took similar times
format_range <- function(x, fmt = NULL) {
  # (times to two significant digits by default)
  if (is.null(fmt)) fmt <- function(v) format_seconds(signif(v, 2))
  x <- fmt(range(x, na.rm = TRUE))
  if (x[1] == x[2]) x[1] else paste0(x[1], "-", x[2])
}
format_mb <- function(x) {
  trimws(formatC(round(x, -1), format = "d", big.mark = ","))
}
# how many times faster than ADMIXTURE (from random values, on the same
# number of cores, without cross-validation), to one significant digit
times_faster <- function(seconds, n_cores = min_cores) {
  signif(time_of("admixture", n_cores) / seconds, 1)
}
# the program that used the least memory (median of its runs from random
# values), with or without cross-validation
has_memory <- any(!is.na(timings$peak_rss_mb))
least_memory <- function(crossval) {
  mb <- timings[timings$crossval == crossval & !is.na(timings$peak_rss_mb), ]
  mb <- tapply(mb$peak_rss_mb, as.character(mb$tool), median)
  program_labels[[tool_program[[names(which.min(mb))]]]]
}
memory_text <- if (has_memory) {
  paste0(
    least_memory(FALSE), " used the least memory without cross-validation, ",
    "and ", least_memory(TRUE), " with it"
  )
} else {
  "The peak memory of the runs was not recorded"
}
# the speed-up of a program from the fewest to the most cores
speed_up_of <- function(tool) {
  formatC(time_of(tool) / time_of(tool, max_cores), format = "f", digits = 1)
}
# the peak memory of the runs of a program from the command line (random
# starts), with or without cross-validation, as a range in MB
memory_of <- function(tool, crossval = FALSE) {
  mb <- timings$peak_rss_mb[timings$tool == tool & timings$crossval == crossval]
  format_range(mb, format_mb)
}
agreement_of <- function(tool, column) {
  agreement[[column]][agreement$run == paste0(tool, "_t", min_cores, "_nocv")]
}
runs_differ_by <- function(tool) {
  diff <- max(agreement$diff_own[agreement$tool == tool])
  if (diff == 0) {
    "identical ancestry proportions"
  } else {
    paste("ancestry proportions that differ by up to", format_diff(diff))
  }
}
# the time taken to start R and load tidygenclust, and to start Julia, load
# OpenADMIXTURE.jl and compile its code: the median difference between the
# runs from the command line and in a session (with the same settings)
startup_of <- function(program) {
  runs <- timings[tool_program[as.character(timings$tool)] == program, ]
  cli <- runs[grepl("_cli$", runs$tool), ]
  session <- runs[!grepl("_cli$", runs$tool), ]
  setting <- function(x) paste(x$n_cores, x$crossval)
  session_seconds <- session$seconds[match(setting(cli), setting(session))]
  median(cli$seconds - session_seconds, na.rm = TRUE)
}
# the runs that ended at a lower log-likelihood than ADMIXTURE (by more than
# 1), and so at another local optimum
local_optima <- agreement %>%
  filter(loglik_diff < -1) %>%
  mutate(
    label = paste0(
      tool_labels[as.character(tool)], " on ", n_cores,
      if_else(n_cores == 1, " core", " cores"),
      if_else(crossval, " with cross-validation", "")
    )
  )
# the largest amount by which a run ended above ADMIXTURE
highest_above <- max(agreement$loglik_diff, na.rm = TRUE)
local_optima_text <- if (nrow(local_optima) == 0 && highest_above <= 1) {
  paste(
    "Here, all the runs reached the log-likelihood of ADMIXTURE, to within",
    "1."
  )
} else if (nrow(local_optima) == 0) {
  paste0(
    "Here, no run ended more than 1 below the log-likelihood of ADMIXTURE, ",
    "and runs of the other programs ended up to ",
    format_diff(highest_above), " above it: ADMIXTURE stopped short of the ",
    "maximum that they reached, by its own convergence criterion, with ",
    "ancestry proportions that differ little from theirs (see the detailed ",
    "results)."
  )
} else {
  paste0(
    "Here, this happened to ", nrow(local_optima),
    if_else(nrow(local_optima) == 1, " run", " runs"), " (",
    paste(local_optima$label, collapse = "; "),
    "), whose log-likelihood is lower than that of ADMIXTURE by up to ",
    format_diff(max(-local_optima$loglik_diff)), "."
  )
}
```

```{r starts, include = FALSE}
# the comparison of the starts: one row per run of the programs that can
# start from an SVD of the genotypes as well as from random values (e.g.
# radmix_cli_svd_s2 for gt_radmix() from an SVD with seed 2)
start_labels <- c(random = "Random", svd = "SVD")
starts <- read.csv(file.path(results_dir, "starts_cli.csv"))
if (!"peak_rss_mb" %in% names(starts)) starts$peak_rss_mb <- NA_real_
starts <- starts %>%
  mutate(
    run = paste0(tool, "_", init, "_s", seed),
    program = factor(tool_program[tool], names(program_labels)),
    init = factor(init, names(start_labels))
  )
starts_cores <- unique(starts$n_cores)
n_seeds <- length(unique(starts$seed))
q_starts <- lapply(
  setNames(starts$run, starts$run),
  function(run) align_q(read_q(run), q_ref)
)
# the highest log-likelihood of all the runs (of both parts of the
# benchmark); a run more than 1 below it ended at another local optimum, or
# stopped short of it
best_loglik <- max(c(timings$loglik, starts$loglik), na.rm = TRUE)
starts <- starts %>%
  mutate(
    loglik_diff = loglik - timings$loglik[timings$run == reference_run],
    below_best = best_loglik - loglik,
    at_best = below_best < 1,
    rmse_ref = vapply(run, function(r) rmse(q_starts[[r]], q_ref), 0)
  )
# the largest difference in ancestry proportions between two runs (of the
# same program from the same start)
largest_spread <- function(runs) {
  if (length(runs) < 2) {
    return(0)
  }
  pairs <- utils::combn(runs, 2)
  max(apply(pairs, 2, function(p) max_diff(q_starts[[p[1]]], q_starts[[p[2]]])))
}
starts_summary <- starts %>%
  group_by(program, init) %>%
  summarise(
    runs = n(),
    seconds_median = median(seconds),
    seconds_min = min(seconds),
    seconds_max = max(seconds),
    iterations = median(iterations),
    at_best = sum(at_best),
    worst = max(below_best),
    spread = largest_spread(run),
    rmse_ref = median(rmse_ref),
    memory = median(peak_rss_mb),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
# the median time of a program from a start
start_seconds <- function(program, init) {
  starts_summary$seconds_median[
    starts_summary$program == program & starts_summary$init == init
  ]
}
# a sentence on a program, for the summary
starts_text <- function(program) {
  paste0(
    format_seconds(signif(start_seconds(program, "svd"), 2)),
    " s from an SVD and ",
    format_seconds(signif(start_seconds(program, "random"), 2)),
    " s from random values"
  )
}
# whether all the runs from both starts reached the same optimum: within 1
# of the highest log-likelihood, or a little further for a program that
# stops earlier by its own convergence criterion (but not more than 10 below,
# which would be another optimum)
worst_by_program <- tapply(starts$below_best, starts$program, max)
worst_by_program <- worst_by_program[!is.na(worst_by_program)]
short_programs <- names(worst_by_program)[worst_by_program >= 1]
starts_optimum_text <- if (all(worst_by_program < 10)) {
  paste0(
    "All these runs reached the same optimum",
    if (length(short_programs) == 0) {
      ", to within 1 of the highest log-likelihood."
    } else {
      paste0(
        ": those of ", knitr::combine_words(program_labels[short_programs]),
        " stopped up to ", format_diff(max(worst_by_program)),
        " below the highest log-likelihood, by their own convergence ",
        "criterion, and those of the other programs within 1 of it."
      )
    }
  )
} else {
  paste0(
    "Some runs ended at other optima (",
    paste0(
      program_labels[as.character(starts_summary$program)], " from ",
      c(random = "random", svd = "SVD")[as.character(starts_summary$init)],
      " starts: ",
      starts_summary$at_best, " of ", starts_summary$runs,
      " at the highest log-likelihood",
      collapse = "; "
    ),
    ")."
  )
}
```

```{r read_ooc, include = FALSE}
# the fits of gt_radmix() on simulated data larger than the memory: one row
# per run (its memory cap and read throughput, time, bytes read, memory),
# with the peak memory of R in it (RssAnon, sampled), and the machine; one
# set of files per data set (mid: about 5 GB; large: 50 GB), absent until
# they are run
read_ooc <- function(name) {
  files <- file.path(
    results_dir, paste0(name, c("_runs.csv", "_memory.csv", "_session.csv"))
  )
  if (!all(file.exists(files))) {
    return(NULL)
  }
  session <- read.csv(files[3])
  runs <- read.csv(files[1]) %>%
    left_join(read.csv(files[2]), by = "run") %>%
    mutate(memory_seconds = seconds[run == "memory"])
  list(
    runs = runs,
    session = session,
    data_gb = as.numeric(session$value[session$item == "backing file bytes"]) /
      1e9
  )
}
ooc <- read_ooc("mid")
ooc_large <- read_ooc("large")
# a cap in GiB, from its systemd form (e.g. "4G")
ooc_gib <- function(cap) as.numeric(sub("G$", "", cap))
format_gb <- function(x) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = 1)
# a run with a memory cap (e.g. "1G") and a read throughput (0: the disk as
# it is), and its time, also as a multiple of the time in memory
ooc_run <- function(d, cap, mbps) {
  d$runs[d$runs$memory_cap == cap & d$runs$read_mbps == mbps, ]
}
ooc_ratio <- function(d, cap, mbps) {
  r <- ooc_run(d, cap, mbps)
  formatC(r$seconds / r$memory_seconds, format = "f", digits = 1)
}
# how much longer than in memory, in percent (e.g. "5% longer")
ooc_longer <- function(d, cap, mbps) {
  r <- ooc_run(d, cap, mbps)
  paste0(round((r$seconds / r$memory_seconds - 1) * 100), "% longer")
}
ooc_time <- function(d, cap, mbps) {
  r <- ooc_run(d, cap, mbps)
  paste0(
    format_seconds(r$seconds), " s, ", ooc_ratio(d, cap, mbps),
    " times its time in memory"
  )
}
# the description of a data set: its size, and how many times larger than
# a cap it is
ooc_data_text <- function(d) {
  r <- d$runs[1, ]
  paste0(
    format(r$n_indiv, big.mark = ","), " individuals typed at ",
    format(r$n_loci, big.mark = ","), " loci (",
    format_gb(d$data_gb), " GB in the backing file of the `gen_tibble`)"
  )
}
# the table of the runs of a data set
ooc_table <- function(d) {
  d$runs %>%
    mutate(
      memory = if_else(memory_cap == "none", "no cap",
        paste(sub("G$", "", memory_cap), "GiB")
      ),
      disk = case_when(
        run == "memory" ~ "(in memory)",
        read_mbps == 0 ~ "SSD",
        TRUE ~ paste(read_mbps, "MB/s")
      ),
      relative = seconds / memory_seconds,
      # the peak of the cgroup (R and the page cache) with a cap, and of the
      # resident memory of R (with the pages of the file it maps) without
      peak = if_else(run == "memory", peak_rss_gb, cgroup_peak_gb)
    ) %>%
    select(memory, disk, seconds, relative, read_gb, peak, peak_anon_gb) %>%
    knitr::kable(
      col.names = c(
        "Memory", "Disk", "Time (s)", "Relative to in memory", "Read (GB)",
        "Peak memory (GB)", "Of which R (GB)"
      ),
      digits = c(0, 0, 0, 1, 0, 2, 2),
      format.args = list(big.mark = ",")
    )
}
if (!is.null(ooc)) {
  ooc_caps <- unique(ooc$runs$memory_cap[ooc$runs$memory_cap != "none"])
  ooc_small <- ooc_caps[which.min(ooc_gib(ooc_caps))]
  ooc_big <- ooc_caps[which.max(ooc_gib(ooc_caps))]
  ooc_mbps <- sort(unique(ooc$runs$read_mbps[ooc$runs$read_mbps > 0]),
    decreasing = TRUE
  )
  ooc_capped <- ooc$runs[ooc$runs$run != "memory", ]
  ooc_summary <- paste0(
    "`gt_radmix()` fitted ", format_gb(ooc$data_gb), " GB of genotypes ",
    "with its memory capped at ", ooc_gib(ooc_small), " GiB, about ",
    round(ooc_gib(ooc_small) * 2^30 / 1e9 / ooc$data_gb * 100, -1),
    "% of the data, in ", ooc_ratio(ooc, ooc_small, 0), " times its time ",
    "in memory on an SSD, with the same results (see ",
    "[Data larger than the memory](#data-larger-than-the-memory))."
  )
}
if (!is.null(ooc_large)) {
  large_cap <- ooc_large$runs$memory_cap[ooc_large$runs$memory_cap != "none"][1]
  large_mbps <- max(ooc_large$runs$read_mbps)
  ooc_summary <- paste0(
    "`gt_radmix()` fitted ", round(ooc_large$data_gb), " GB of genotypes (",
    format(ooc_large$runs$n_indiv[1], big.mark = ","), " individuals ",
    "typed at ", format(ooc_large$runs$n_loci[1], big.mark = ","),
    " loci) with its memory capped at ", ooc_gib(large_cap), " GiB, a ",
    "sixth of the data, on an SSD, with the same results, taking ",
    ooc_longer(ooc_large, large_cap, 0), " than in memory (",
    ooc_longer(ooc, ooc_small, 0), " on ", format_gb(ooc$data_gb),
    " GB with a fifth of the data in memory; see ",
    "[Data larger than the memory](#data-larger-than-the-memory))."
  )
}
```

## Summary

The five programs estimated the ancestry proportions of `r n_indiv`
individuals of the HGDP, typed at `r format(n_loci, big.mark = ",")` loci,
for K = `r k` ancestral populations (see [The data](#the-data)). On this
dataset:

- **The same answer.** All the programs found the same ancestry
  proportions: on `r min_cores` core without cross-validation, those of
  the other programs differ from those of ADMIXTURE by at most
  `r format_diff(max(agreement$diff_ref[agreement$n_cores == min_cores & !agreement$crossval]))`
  (see [Do the programs find the same ancestry proportions?](#do-the-programs-find-the-same-ancestry-proportions)).
  Across numbers of cores, with and without cross-validation,
  `gt_radmix()` gives `r runs_differ_by("radmix")`, ADMIXTURE
  `r runs_differ_by("admixture")`, fastmixture
  `r runs_differ_by("fastmixture")`, ADAMIXTURE
  `r runs_differ_by("adamixture")`, and OpenADMIXTURE.jl (without
  cross-validation) `r runs_differ_by("openadmixture")`.
- **fastmixture is much faster than ADMIXTURE.** It makes good use of
  several cores (its time fell `r speed_up_of("fastmixture")` times from
  `r min_cores` to `r max_cores` cores, against
  `r speed_up_of("admixture")` times for ADMIXTURE), and from an SVD of
  the genotypes, its default start, it took a median of
  `r format_seconds(signif(start_seconds("fastmixture", "svd"), 2))` s on
  `r starts_cores` cores, about
  `r times_faster(start_seconds("fastmixture", "svd"), starts_cores)` times
  faster than ADMIXTURE from random values.
- **`gt_radmix()` and ADAMIXTURE run at similar speeds.** From random
  values, they took
  `r format_range(c(time_of("radmix_cli"), time_of("adamixture")))` s on
  `r min_cores` core and
  `r format_range(c(time_of("radmix_cli", max_cores), time_of("adamixture", max_cores)))`
  s on `r max_cores` cores (from the command line), about
  `r times_faster(mean(c(time_of("radmix_cli"), time_of("adamixture"))))`
  and
  `r times_faster(mean(c(time_of("radmix_cli", max_cores), time_of("adamixture", max_cores))), max_cores)`
  times faster than ADMIXTURE. The differences between them are small,
  and depend on the machine (see
  [How long do they take?](#how-long-do-they-take)).
- **SVD starts save time.** On `r starts_cores` cores, with `r n_seeds`
  seeds, `gt_radmix()` took `r starts_text("radmix")`; ADAMIXTURE
  `r starts_text("adamixture")`; and fastmixture
  `r starts_text("fastmixture")` (median times from the command line).
  `r starts_optimum_text`
- **Memory.** `r memory_text` (see
  [How much memory do they use?](#how-much-memory-do-they-use)).
`r if (!is.null(ooc)) paste0("- **Data larger than the memory.** ", ooc_summary)`

## Random starts

### Do the programs find the same ancestry proportions?

All the programs maximise the same likelihood, but each starts from its
own random values and stops according to its own convergence criterion.
Each run is compared with ADMIXTURE on `r min_cores` core without
cross-validation, after matching its clusters to those of ADMIXTURE
(the [detailed results](#detailed-results) give the numbers of each run):

```{r plot_agreement, echo = FALSE, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 2.6}
measure_labels <- c(
  loglik_diff = "Log-likelihood minus ADMIXTURE's",
  rmse_ref = "RMSE from ADMIXTURE's proportions"
)
agreement %>%
  mutate(
    program = factor(
      tool_program[as.character(tool)],
      rev(names(program_labels))
    )
  ) %>%
  select(program, loglik_diff, rmse_ref) %>%
  pivot_longer(c(loglik_diff, rmse_ref), names_to = "measure") %>%
  mutate(measure = factor(measure, names(measure_labels))) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = value, y = program, colour = program)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "grey60", linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_point(
    size = 2.5, alpha = 0.7,
    position = position_jitter(width = 0, height = 0.12, seed = 1)
  ) +
  facet_wrap(
    ~measure,
    scales = "free_x",
    labeller = labeller(measure = measure_labels)
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = scales::breaks_extended(n = 3),
    labels = function(x) {
      format(x, scientific = FALSE, drop0trailing = TRUE, trim = TRUE)
    }
  ) +
  scale_y_discrete(labels = program_labels) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = program_colours, guide = "none") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
```

Each point is a run (on each number of cores, with and without
cross-validation, and, for `gt_radmix()` and OpenADMIXTURE.jl, from the
command line and in a session).

Each program was run once for each number of cores, from a single random
start (with seed 1, but each program draws its own random values), so a
run can end at another local optimum of the likelihood, with a lower
log-likelihood and different ancestry proportions.
`r local_optima_text`

The ancestry proportions from each program (on `r min_cores` core, without
cross-validation, and in a session for `gt_radmix()` and
OpenADMIXTURE.jl), with the individuals grouped by region and population:

```{r plot_q, echo = FALSE, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 6.8}
# the regions of the HGDP, from west to east
region_levels <- c(
  "Africa", "Middle_East", "Europe", "Central_South_Asia", "East_Asia",
  "Oceania", "America"
)
# the individuals are ordered by region and population, and, within each
# population, by the ancestry (in the reference) from its main cluster
main_cluster <- vapply(
  split(seq_len(nrow(q_ref)), individuals$population),
  function(rows) which.max(colMeans(q_ref[rows, , drop = FALSE])),
  integer(1)
)
main_ancestry <- q_ref[cbind(
  seq_len(nrow(q_ref)),
  main_cluster[individuals$population]
)]
indiv_order <- order(
  factor(individuals$region, region_levels),
  individuals$population,
  -main_ancestry
)
q_long <- bind_rows(lapply(names(program_labels), function(tool) {
  q <- q_aligned[[paste0(tool, "_t", min_cores, "_nocv")]][indiv_order, ]
  data.frame(
    tool = tool,
    individual = rep(seq_len(nrow(q)), k),
    region = rep(individuals$region[indiv_order], k),
    cluster = factor(rep(seq_len(k), each = nrow(q))),
    proportion = as.vector(q)
  )
})) %>%
  mutate(
    tool = factor(tool, names(program_labels)),
    region = factor(region, region_levels)
  )
# one colour per cluster (from the Okabe-Ito palette)
cluster_colours <- c(
  "#E69F00", "#56B4E9", "#009E73", "#F0E442", "#0072B2", "#D55E00",
  "#CC79A7", "#999999"
)
ggplot(q_long, aes(x = individual, y = proportion, fill = cluster)) +
  geom_col(width = 1) +
  facet_grid(
    tool ~ region,
    scales = "free_x",
    space = "free_x",
    labeller = labeller(
      tool = program_labels,
      region = function(x) gsub("_", " ", x)
    )
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = cluster_colours, guide = "none") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = NULL, expand = c(0, 0)) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = NULL, expand = c(0, 0)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    panel.spacing.x = unit(0.1, "lines"),
    strip.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 0),
    strip.text.y = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 0)
  )
```

### How long do they take?

The times of ADMIXTURE, fastmixture and ADAMIXTURE are those of runs from
the command line: each run is a new process, which starts the program, reads
the bed file and writes the estimates of Q and P to text files (ADAMIXTURE
also always draws a plot of the ancestry proportions, which is included in
its time). `gt_radmix()` and
OpenADMIXTURE.jl are timed in the same way, with `Rscript` and `julia`
(command line), and also in a session, where R or Julia is already running
with the package loaded:

- for `gt_radmix()`, the time of reading the bed file into a `gen_tibble`
  (and its backing file), running `gt_radmix()`, and saving the resulting
  `gt_admix` object, with Q and P, to an RDS file. In an analysis with
  several values of K, or several runs, the `gen_tibble` would only be read
  once;
- for OpenADMIXTURE.jl, the time of its fit (including reading the bed file
  and writing Q and P), measured in Julia after a first, untimed run on a
  small subset of the data. Julia compiles the code of a function the first
  time it is called, so this is the time of a fit in a Julia session in
  which OpenADMIXTURE.jl has already been used.

```{r plot_timings, echo = FALSE, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5}
# one type of line per way of running it
setting_labels <- c(
  cli = "Command line",
  session = "Session (R or Julia)"
)
timings %>%
  mutate(
    program = factor(tool_program[as.character(tool)], names(program_labels)),
    setting = factor(
      if_else(tool %in% c("radmix", "openadmixture"), "session", "cli"),
      names(setting_labels)
    ),
    crossval = if_else(
      crossval,
      "With cross-validation",
      "Without cross-validation"
    ),
    crossval = factor(
      crossval,
      c("Without cross-validation", "With cross-validation")
    )
  ) %>%
  ggplot(aes(
    x = n_cores, y = seconds, colour = program, linetype = setting,
    group = tool
  )) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5) +
  facet_wrap(~crossval) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = sort(unique(timings$n_cores))) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  scale_colour_manual(values = program_colours, labels = program_labels) +
  scale_linetype_manual(
    values = c(cli = "solid", session = "22"),
    labels = setting_labels
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Cores", y = "Time (s, log scale)", colour = NULL, linetype = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "top",
    legend.box = "vertical",
    legend.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0)
  )
```

(The times and speed-ups of each run are in the
[detailed results](#detailed-results).) Starting R and loading `tidygenclust` adds about
`r format_seconds(startup_of("radmix"))` s to each run of `gt_radmix()`
from the command line. Starting Julia, loading OpenADMIXTURE.jl and
compiling its code adds about
`r format_seconds(startup_of("openadmixture"))` s to each run of
OpenADMIXTURE.jl (these are the median differences between the runs from
the command line and in a session).

ADMIXTURE gained little from more cores. fastmixture, with its accelerated
EM updates over mini-batches of the loci, made good use of them: its time
fell `r speed_up_of("fastmixture")` times from `r min_cores` to
`r max_cores` cores, and on `r max_cores` cores it was much faster than
ADMIXTURE, even from random values (and faster still from an SVD, its
default, see [SVD and random starts](#svd-and-random-starts)).
`gt_radmix()` and ADAMIXTURE, which both take block-wise Newton steps with
quasi-Newton acceleration, as ADMIXTURE does, in compiled multithreaded
code, took similar times on every number of cores, with and without
cross-validation. OpenADMIXTURE.jl, which uses the same algorithm, took
`r format_seconds(time_of("openadmixture", max_cores))` s on
`r max_cores` cores in a Julia session.

Differences of a few tens of percent between programs are not meaningful
here. Each run was done once, and the relative speeds of the programs
depend on the machine, the compiler and the libraries. For example,
ADAMIXTURE computes its main sums as matrix products with an optimised
BLAS library (OpenBLAS, or Accelerate on macOS), which can use the wider
vector instructions of some servers (AVX-512) and the matrix units of
Apple processors. `gt_radmix()` uses its own loops, compiled for AVX2 only
on Linux with GCC 12 or later, and multithreaded only where R supports
OpenMP (which the CRAN builds of R for macOS do not, without extra set-up).

### How much memory do they use?

```{r memory_text, include = FALSE}
# the memory of a program in the text (random starts, from the command
# line), without and with cross-validation
memory_both <- function(tool) {
  if (!has_memory) {
    return("(not recorded)")
  }
  without <- memory_of(tool)
  with <- memory_of(tool, TRUE)
  if (without == with) {
    return(paste(without, "MB in both"))
  }
  paste0(without, " and ", with, " MB")
}
```

The peak resident memory of each run from the command line was recorded
with `/usr/bin/time` (the [detailed results](#detailed-results) give it
for each run). From random values, without and with cross-validation,
ADAMIXTURE used `r memory_both("adamixture")`; fastmixture
`r memory_both("fastmixture")`; ADMIXTURE `r memory_both("admixture")`;
and `gt_radmix()` `r memory_both("radmix_cli")`, including R and its
packages, and the parts of the backing file of the `gen_tibble` held in
memory. OpenADMIXTURE.jl, which has no cross-validation, used
`r if (has_memory) memory_of("openadmixture_cli") else "(not recorded)"`
MB, including Julia. ADAMIXTURE keeps the genotypes in a 2-bit packed
encoding, which keeps its memory low without cross-validation, and
fastmixture used about as much memory with cross-validation as without.
`gt_radmix()` reads the genotypes from the backing file of the `gen_tibble`,
which the system keeps in memory when it fits; when it does not,
`gt_radmix()` reads it in chunks (see
[Data larger than the memory](#data-larger-than-the-memory)).

### Cross-validation errors

The cross-validation errors did not depend on the number of cores. On
`r min_cores` core, they were `r cv_of("radmix_cli")` with `gt_radmix()`,
`r cv_of("admixture")` with ADMIXTURE, `r cv_of("adamixture")` with
ADAMIXTURE and `r cv_of("fastmixture")` with fastmixture (see the
[detailed results](#detailed-results) for all the runs).

OpenADMIXTURE.jl has no cross-validation. ADMIXTURE and `gt_radmix()`
compute the same cross-validation error (Alexander and Lange 2011): they
hold out a fold of the genotypes, refit the model on the others, and average
the deviance of the held-out genotypes.
They draw the folds differently, so their errors are close but not
identical. fastmixture averages the same deviance, but holds out a fold of
the individuals rather than of the genotypes. The allele frequencies come
from the other individuals, but the ancestry of the held-out individuals is
estimated from their own genotypes, the same genotypes on which the error is
then computed. Its errors can be compared between values of K, but not with
those of the other programs. ADAMIXTURE also averages the deviance of
held-out genotypes, but it refits the model on each fold with only 5
iterations, starting from the estimates on all the genotypes, so its errors
are close to those of ADMIXTURE and `gt_radmix()`, but not identical.

## SVD and random starts

`gt_radmix()`, fastmixture and ADAMIXTURE can start from a truncated SVD of
the genotypes, followed by alternating least squares (ALS) on its factors,
as well as from random values. fastmixture and ADAMIXTURE start from the
SVD by default, `gt_radmix()` from random values (the SVD is an option,
`init = "svd"`). Each of the three programs was run from both starts with
seeds 1 to `r n_seeds`, on `r starts_cores` cores, without
cross-validation, from the command line:

```{r plot_starts, echo = FALSE, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 2.8}
start_colours <- c(random = "#c1661c", svd = "#3b5ba5")
start_programs <- c("radmix", "fastmixture", "adamixture")
# one row per program, with the runs from the two starts just above and
# below it
starts_plot <- starts %>%
  mutate(
    row = match(as.character(program), rev(start_programs)) +
      if_else(init == "svd", -0.15, 0.15)
  )
starts_panel <- function(column, title, x_scale, show_y = FALSE) {
  ggplot(starts_plot, aes(x = .data[[column]], y = row, colour = .data$init)) +
    geom_point(size = 2.2, alpha = 0.7) +
    x_scale +
    scale_y_continuous(
      breaks = seq_along(start_programs),
      labels = program_labels[rev(start_programs)],
      limits = c(0.6, length(start_programs) + 0.4)
    ) +
    scale_colour_manual(
      values = start_colours,
      labels = c(random = "Random start", svd = "SVD start")
    ) +
    labs(title = title, x = NULL, y = NULL, colour = NULL) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
      plot.title = element_text(size = 10),
      axis.text.y = if (show_y) element_text() else element_blank()
    )
}
format_axis <- function(x) {
  format(x, scientific = FALSE, drop0trailing = TRUE, trim = TRUE)
}
patchwork::wrap_plots(
  starts_panel(
    "seconds", "Time (s)", scale_x_log10(labels = format_axis),
    show_y = TRUE
  ),
  starts_panel("iterations", "Iterations", scale_x_log10(labels = format_axis)),
  starts_panel(
    "below_best", "Below the best log-likelihood",
    scale_x_continuous(
      trans = scales::pseudo_log_trans(sigma = 0.01, base = 10),
      breaks = c(0, 0.1, 1, 10, 100, 1000, 1e4, 1e5, 1e6),
      labels = format_axis,
      expand = expansion(mult = 0.1)
    )
  ) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 1, colour = "grey60", linetype = "dashed"),
  nrow = 1
) +
  patchwork::plot_layout(guides = "collect") &
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

Each point is a run. Time and iterations are on log scales; the
iterations of a program count its own steps, so they can be compared
between its two starts but not between programs. The right panel shows how
far the log-likelihood of each run is below the highest of all the runs of
the benchmark: the runs left of the dashed line (within 1 of it) reached
the same optimum. `r starts_optimum_text`

The time of `gt_radmix()` from the command line includes starting R and
loading `tidygenclust` (about `r format_seconds(startup_of("radmix"))` s).
Its SVD needs no imputation of the missing genotypes: it is computed by
`tidypopgen::gt_pca()`, which, as PLINK 1.9 does, compares each pair of
individuals over the loci genotyped in both.

## Data larger than the memory

`gt_radmix()` reads the genotypes from the backing file of the
`gen_tibble`, which it maps into memory: the system keeps as much of the
file in memory as it can (in its page cache), and reads the rest from the
disk when it is needed. Each iteration of `gt_radmix()` goes through all the
genotypes several times, so data that do not fit in memory could be read
from the disk many times over in each pass. When the backing file is larger
than the memory available to R, `gt_radmix()` therefore streams it: each
pass over the genotypes reads the file in chunks, alternating its direction
from one pass to the next (so that the end of one pass and the start of the
next find their chunks still in memory), and asks the system to read the
next chunk while the current one is processed. The results are identical to
those of the same fit in memory. With 8,192 individuals or more, as here,
the passes over the individuals take the loci in chunks in memory too, which
is faster, so the fits in memory and out of it below do the same work in the
same order.

`r if (is.null(ooc)) "*(The runs of this section have not been done yet.)*"`

```{r ooc_intro, include = FALSE, eval = !is.null(ooc)}
ooc_intro <- paste0(
  "To measure what this costs, `gt_radmix()` was run on simulated ",
  "genotypes of ", ooc_data_text(ooc), ", for K = ", ooc$runs$k[1],
  " on ", ooc$runs$n_cores[1], " cores (see [How the benchmark was ",
  "run](#data-larger-than-the-memory-1)): in memory, and then with the ",
  "memory of R, page cache included, capped at ", ooc_gib(ooc_big),
  " GiB (a little less than the data) and at ", ooc_gib(ooc_small),
  " GiB (about a fifth of them), reading from the SSD of the machine and ",
  "from the same disk with its reads throttled to ",
  knitr::combine_words(ooc_mbps), " MB/s, the speeds of a slower SSD and ",
  "of a hard disk:"
)
```

`r if (!is.null(ooc)) ooc_intro`

```{r table_ooc, echo = FALSE, eval = !is.null(ooc)}
ooc_table(ooc)
```

```{r ooc_results, include = FALSE, eval = !is.null(ooc)}
ooc_results <- paste0(
  if (length(unique(ooc$runs$loglik)) == 1) {
    "All the fits reached the same log-likelihood, with the same ancestry proportions. "
  } else {
    "The fits did not all reach the same log-likelihood. "
  },
  "On the SSD, the fit took ", ooc_time(ooc, ooc_big, 0), ", with ",
  ooc_gib(ooc_big), " GiB, and ", ooc_time(ooc, ooc_small, 0), ", with ",
  ooc_gib(ooc_small), " GiB. On the slower disks, the time is set by the ",

    ooc_run(ooc, ooc_small, ooc_mbps[1])$read_gb * 1000 / ooc_mbps[1]
  ),
  " s at ", ooc_mbps[1], " MB/s), and took ",
  ooc_time(ooc, ooc_small, ooc_mbps[1]), ", at ", ooc_mbps[1], " MB/s, and ",
  ooc_time(ooc, ooc_small, ooc_mbps[2]), ", at ", ooc_mbps[2], " MB/s. ",
  "With a cap, the memory of the process (R and the page cache, the peak ",
  "memory in the table) stayed within the cap: the page cache fills the ",
  "room R leaves, while R itself used at most ",
  formatC(max(ooc_capped$peak_anon_gb), format = "f", digits = 2), " GB. ",
  "Without a cap, the peak memory is that of R and of the pages of the file ",
  "it mapped, the whole file."
)
```

`r if (!is.null(ooc)) ooc_results`

The throttle limits the throughput of the disk, not its latency, so it
mimics a slower disk only in part.

```{r ooc_large_text, include = FALSE, eval = !is.null(ooc_large)}

large_run_slow <- ooc_run(ooc_large, large_cap, large_mbps)
ooc_large_intro <- paste0(

  format_gb(as.numeric(ooc_large$session$value[
    ooc_large$session$item == "bed file bytes"
  ]) / 1e9), " GB even as a bed file, with 2 bits per genotype, ",
  "`gt_radmix()` was run in memory and with its memory capped at ",
  ooc_gib(large_cap), " GiB, about a sixth of the data, on the SSD and ",
  "at ", large_mbps, " MB/s:"
)
ooc_large_results <- paste0(
  if (length(unique(ooc_large$runs$loglik)) == 1) {
    "The three fits reached the same log-likelihood. "
  } else {
    "The fits did not all reach the same log-likelihood. "
  },
  "In memory, the fit took ",
  format_seconds(large_run_ssd$memory_seconds), " s (",
  round(large_run_ssd$memory_seconds / 60), " minutes), with the whole ",
  "file in memory. Capped at ", ooc_gib(large_cap), " GiB, it took ",

  "disk at ", formatC(large_run_ssd$read_gb / large_run_ssd$seconds,

  ), " GB/s on average (in memory, the same passes went through the data ",

    format = "f", digits = 1
  ), " GB/s), and ",
  ooc_time(ooc_large, large_cap, large_mbps), ", at ", large_mbps,
  " MB/s, as long as it takes to read its ",
  format(signif(large_run_slow$read_gb, 2), big.mark = ","), " GB at that ",

  " s). R itself used at most ",
  formatC(max(ooc_large$runs$peak_anon_gb), format = "f", digits = 2),
  " GB."
)
```

`r if (!is.null(ooc_large)) ooc_large_intro`

```{r table_ooc_large, echo = FALSE, eval = !is.null(ooc_large)}
ooc_table(ooc_large)
```

`r if (!is.null(ooc_large)) ooc_large_results`

## Detailed results

### Agreement between the programs (random starts)

```{r table_agreement, echo = FALSE}
agreement %>%
  arrange(tool, n_cores, crossval) %>%
  mutate(
    tool = tool_labels[as.character(tool)],
    crossval = if_else(crossval, "yes", "no"),
    loglik = formatC(loglik, format = "f", digits = 2, big.mark = ","),
    across(c(loglik_diff, diff_own, rmse_ref, diff_ref), format_diff)
  ) %>%
  select(
    tool, n_cores, crossval, loglik, loglik_diff, diff_own, rmse_ref, diff_ref
  ) %>%
  knitr::kable(
    col.names = c(
      "Program", "Cores", "CV", "Log-likelihood", "Difference",
      "Largest difference (same program)", "RMSE (ADMIXTURE)",
      "Largest difference (ADMIXTURE)"
    ),
    align = "lllrrrrr",
    caption = paste0(
      "Log-likelihood of each run (fastmixture and ADAMIXTURE report it with ",
      "one decimal), ",
      "and its difference from that of ADMIXTURE on ", min_cores, " core ",
      "without cross-validation (CV; positive when higher). ",
      "Largest absolute difference between the ancestry proportions of each ",
      "run and those of the same program on ", min_cores, " core without ",
      "CV, and root mean square error (RMSE) and largest absolute difference ",
      "from those of ADMIXTURE on ", min_cores, " core without CV. The Q ",
      "matrices are stored with 6 decimals, so differences smaller than ",
      "1e-6 do not show."
    )
  )
```

### Times (random starts)

```{r table_timings, echo = FALSE}
timings %>%
  group_by(tool, crossval) %>%
  mutate(speed_up = seconds[n_cores == min_cores] / seconds) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(tool, n_cores, crossval, seconds, speed_up, peak_rss_mb) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = crossval,
    values_from = c(seconds, speed_up, peak_rss_mb)
  ) %>%
  arrange(tool, n_cores) %>%
  mutate(
    tool = tool_labels[as.character(tool)],
    across(
      starts_with("seconds"),
      ~ if_else(is.na(.x), "-", format_seconds(.x))
    ),
    across(
      starts_with("speed_up"),
      ~ if_else(is.na(.x), "-", formatC(.x, format = "f", digits = 1))
    ),
    across(
      starts_with("peak_rss_mb"),
      ~ if_else(is.na(.x), "-", format_mb(.x))
    )
  ) %>%
  select(
    tool, n_cores, seconds_FALSE, speed_up_FALSE, peak_rss_mb_FALSE,
    seconds_TRUE, speed_up_TRUE, peak_rss_mb_TRUE
  ) %>%
  knitr::kable(
    col.names = c(
      "Program", "Cores", "Time (s)", "Speed-up", "Memory (MB)",
      "Time with CV (s)", "Speed-up with CV", "Memory with CV (MB)"
    ),
    align = "lrrrrrrr",
    caption = paste0(
      "Time (s) taken by each run, without and with cross-validation (CV), ",
      "speed-up relative to the run of the same program on ", min_cores,
      " core, and peak resident memory (MB; recorded for the runs from the ",
      "command line). OpenADMIXTURE.jl has no cross-validation."
    )
  )
```

### Cross-validation errors (random starts)

```{r table_cv, echo = FALSE}
timings %>%
  filter(crossval) %>%
  arrange(tool, n_cores) %>%
  mutate(
    tool = tool_labels[as.character(tool)],
    cv_error = formatC(cv_error, format = "f", digits = 5)
  ) %>%
  select(tool, n_cores, cv_error) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = n_cores, values_from = cv_error) %>%
  knitr::kable(
    col.names = c(
      "Program",
      paste(
        sort(unique(timings$n_cores)),
        if_else(sort(unique(timings$n_cores)) == 1, "core", "cores")
      )
    ),
    align = paste0("l", strrep("r", length(unique(timings$n_cores)))),
    caption = "Cross-validation error of each program, on each number of cores."
  )
```

### Random and SVD starts

```{r table_starts, echo = FALSE}
starts_summary %>%
  arrange(program, init) %>%
  mutate(
    program = program_labels[as.character(program)],
    init = start_labels[as.character(init)],
    seconds = paste0(
      format_seconds(seconds_median), " (", format_seconds(seconds_min),
      "-", format_seconds(seconds_max), ")"
    ),
    at_best = paste(at_best, "of", runs),
    across(c(worst, spread, rmse_ref), format_diff),
    memory = if_else(is.na(memory), "-", format_mb(memory))
  ) %>%
  select(
    program, init, seconds, iterations, memory, at_best, worst, spread,
    rmse_ref
  ) %>%
  knitr::kable(
    col.names = c(
      "Program", "Start", "Time (s)", "Iterations", "Memory (MB)",
      "At the best", "Largest shortfall", "Largest difference between runs",
      "RMSE (ADMIXTURE)"
    ),
    align = "llrrrrrrr",
    caption = paste0(
      "Median time (s; range in brackets) and number of iterations of the ",
      n_seeds, " runs of each program from each start, and their median ",
      "peak resident memory (MB); number of runs that ",
      "reached the highest log-likelihood of all the runs of the benchmark ",
      "(to within 1), and the largest shortfall from it; largest absolute ",
      "difference between the ancestry proportions of two runs of the same ",
      "program from the same start; and median root mean square error ",
      "(RMSE) of the ancestry proportions from those of ADMIXTURE on ",
      min_cores, " core without cross-validation. The numbers of iterations ",
      "are not comparable between programs (see ",
      "[Running the programs from the command line]",
      "(#running-the-programs-from-the-command-line))."
    )
  )
```

# How the benchmark was run

The benchmark is run with scripts in `vignettes/articles/code` (in the
source code of the package). The first prepares the data. The second runs
the programs from the command line: ADMIXTURE, fastmixture, ADAMIXTURE,
and `gt_radmix()` and OpenADMIXTURE.jl with two more scripts, which
`Rscript` and `julia` run. The last runs `gt_radmix()` in an R session. The results are read here from
`vignettes/articles/data/admixture_benchmark`. Each run is done once, as the
full runs take long enough for the variation between repeated runs to be
small. The code shown below is taken from these scripts. Timings depend on
the machine (see [Machine and software](#machine-and-software)), the
compiler and the libraries: large differences between the programs should
hold on other machines, but small ones need not (see
[How long do they take?](#how-long-do-they-take)).

## The data

The data are those of the HGDP used in the benchmark of `tidypopgen`
(1043 individuals typed at about 650,000 loci), downloaded from Zenodo:

```{r download, eval = FALSE}
```

and prepared as recommended in the manual of ADMIXTURE. The steps are the
same as in the analyses of the HGDP with `tidygenclust`:

```{r filter, eval = FALSE}
```

```{r ld-clumping, eval = FALSE}
```

All the programs are run on this bed file. A small subset of it is also
saved, to check the scripts quickly (see
[Running the benchmark again](#running-the-benchmark-again)):

```{r quick-data, eval = FALSE}
```

## Running the programs from the command line

All the programs are run from the command line with the same settings:

```{bash cli-settings, eval = FALSE}
```

Each program is run on `r cores_text` cores (with `-j` in ADMIXTURE,
`--threads` in fastmixture, `-t` and `OMP_NUM_THREADS` in ADAMIXTURE,
`n_cores` in `gt_radmix()` and the number of threads of Julia for
OpenADMIXTURE.jl), with and without cross-validation (with `--cv` in
ADMIXTURE, fastmixture and ADAMIXTURE, and `crossval` in `gt_radmix()`;
OpenADMIXTURE.jl has none), from random values or from an SVD of the
genotypes (with `--random-init` in fastmixture, `--init random` or
`--init svd` in ADAMIXTURE, and `init` in `gt_radmix()`), with these
functions:

```{bash cli-functions, eval = FALSE}
```

and the time, Q matrix, log-likelihood, cross-validation error and number of
iterations of each run are saved:

```{bash cli-runs, eval = FALSE}
```

The programs are first run from random values, on each number of cores,
with and without cross-validation:

```{bash cli-random, eval = FALSE}
```

and then `gt_radmix()`, fastmixture and ADAMIXTURE from both starts, with
several seeds:

```{bash cli-starts, eval = FALSE}
```

From the command line, `gt_radmix()` is run by this R script (with
`Rscript`), which reads the same bed file into a `gen_tibble`, runs
`gt_radmix()`, and saves the result to an RDS file:

```{r r-cli, eval = FALSE}
```

and OpenADMIXTURE.jl by this Julia script (with `julia`), which runs it on
all the loci, without its selection of ancestry informative markers, with
its default settings (which `gt_radmix()` follows, except for its
convergence threshold, see below):

```{r julia-run, eval = FALSE, lang = "julia"}
```

## Running gt_radmix() in an R session

`gt_radmix()` runs on a `gen_tibble`. Its parallel loops use OpenMP,
with `n_cores` threads. From random values, it only calls BLAS for small
systems of K equations; BLAS is limited to the cores of each run:

```{r r-packages, eval = FALSE}
```

It is run from random values, with the same settings as the other
programs:

```{r r-settings, eval = FALSE}
```

Each run reads the same bed file into a `gen_tibble`, runs
`gt_radmix()`, and saves the result to an RDS file:

```{r r-runs, eval = FALSE}
```

Each program stops when its own default convergence criterion is met.
ADMIXTURE stops when the log-likelihood increases by less than 1e-4 between
iterations. fastmixture checks every 5 iterations, and stops when the
log-likelihood, divided by the number of observed genotypes, has increased
by less than 1e-9. ADAMIXTURE, with its default solver (BR-QN; it also
offers the Adam-EM algorithm of its paper), stops when the log-likelihood
changes by less than 0.1 between iterations. `gt_radmix()` stops when the
relative change in the log-likelihood is less than 1e-8, and OpenADMIXTURE.jl
when it is less than 1e-7. The numbers of iterations are not comparable either. An
iteration of fastmixture is a pass of accelerated EM updates, first over
mini-batches of the loci. An iteration of ADMIXTURE, ADAMIXTURE,
`gt_radmix()` and OpenADMIXTURE.jl updates all the parameters with
block-wise Newton steps. From random values, ADMIXTURE, ADAMIXTURE,
`gt_radmix()` and OpenADMIXTURE.jl first refine them with a few EM steps.
From an SVD (computed by `tidypopgen::gt_pca()` for `gt_radmix()`),
fastmixture, ADAMIXTURE and `gt_radmix()` start from the
solution of alternating least squares on its factors; the ALS step of
`gt_radmix()` is adapted from ADAMIXTURE (`src/radmix_als.cpp`, see
`inst/COPYRIGHTS`), and both ADAMIXTURE and `gt_radmix()` keep the best of
three such solutions by log-likelihood.

## Data larger than the memory

The genotypes of [Data larger than the memory](#data-larger-than-the-memory)
are simulated, in blocks of loci on several cores, straight into the backing
file of a file-backed matrix (from `bigstatsr`), written as a bed file and
read into a `gen_tibble`, by `code/admixture_benchmark_large_data.R`. Its
sizes and paths can be set with environment variables (the data are not
part of the repository):

```{r large-setup, eval = FALSE}
```

Five ancestral populations, and five sampled ones, each mostly of one
ancestry:

```{r large-simulate, eval = FALSE}
```

```{r large-bed, eval = FALSE}
```

```{r large-gen-tibble, eval = FALSE}
```

Each fit is run by `code/admixture_benchmark_large_fit.R`, which records
its time, the bytes it read from the disk, its memory, whether
`gt_radmix()` streamed the data, and how close its ancestry proportions are
to the simulated ones:

```{r large-fit, eval = FALSE}
```

```{r large-check, eval = FALSE}
```

The fits are run by `code/admixture_benchmark_large.sh`: the first in
memory, the others under a memory cap (a transient scope of systemd, on
Linux with cgroups v2, which also counts the page cache), from a cold page
cache, on the disk as it is or with its reads throttled (which needs root):

```{bash large-runs, eval = FALSE}
```

For the data of this article (`r if (!is.null(ooc)) format_gb(ooc$data_gb) else "about 5"` GB), from `vignettes/articles`:

```sh
cd vignettes/articles
LARGE_DIR=data/mid LARGE_N_INDIV=50000 LARGE_N_LOCI=100000 \
  Rscript code/admixture_benchmark_large_data.R
sudo -v
LARGE_DIR=data/mid LARGE_NAME=mid LARGE_MEMORY_CAPS="4G 1G" \
  LARGE_READ_MBPS="0 500 150" taskset -c 0-7 \
  bash code/admixture_benchmark_large.sh
```

and for the larger data (`r if (!is.null(ooc_large)) round(ooc_large$data_gb) else 50` GB; the defaults of the scripts), which take
about 120 GB of disk while they are simulated:

```sh
cd vignettes/articles
Rscript code/admixture_benchmark_large_data.R
sudo -v
taskset -c 0-7 bash code/admixture_benchmark_large.sh
```

## From the results to the tables and plots

The results are read, and the Q matrices aligned and compared, with this
code:

```{r, ref.label = c("results_packages", "read_results", "align_q", "agreement"), eval = FALSE}
```

## Running the benchmark again

To run the benchmark again (e.g. after changing `tidygenclust`, or on
another machine), install `tidygenclust` with `R CMD INSTALL`, rather than
loading it with `devtools::load_all()`, which compiles its C++ code without
optimisation. Also install ADMIXTURE, fastmixture and ADAMIXTURE, e.g. in
the conda environment created by `tgc_tools_install()`, and OpenADMIXTURE.jl,
in the
conda environment created (from the root of the package) by:

```sh
bash data-raw/radmix/setup_julia_env.sh
```

Then run, from `vignettes/articles`, on an otherwise idle machine with at
least `r max_cores` cores (the largest number of cores tested, set by
`cores` in the scripts). On a processor with performance and efficiency
cores, confine the runs to the performance cores (e.g. with `taskset -c 0-7`
before `bash` and `Rscript` on Linux):

```sh
cd vignettes/articles
Rscript code/admixture_benchmark_data.R
conda activate ctidygenclust
bash code/admixture_benchmark_cli.sh
Rscript code/admixture_benchmark_radmix.R
```

The first script downloads and prepares the data in `data/hgdp`, which is
not part of the repository, and only needs to be run once. The other two
overwrite the results in `data/admixture_benchmark`; then render this
article again. With the argument `quick`, the last two scripts run
everything on the small subset of the data, to check them in less time.
They then save their results in `data/admixture_benchmark_quick`, which this
article can be rendered on with:

```r
rmarkdown::render(
  "admixture_benchmark.Rmd",
  params = list(results_dir = "data/admixture_benchmark_quick")
)
```
